title: Profiteroles
subtitle: Choux pastry puffs with cream and chocolate sauce
excerpt: Light choux pastry buns baked hollow, filled with cold whipped cream, and piled on a plate with warm dark chocolate sauce poured over. A French classic that became a British restaurant staple.

recipe.sourceNotes: Profiteroles are small balls of choux pastry (pâte à choux), which is a cooked paste of butter, water, flour, and eggs that puffs dramatically when baked. The technique for choux was established in French cuisine in the 17th and 18th centuries. Profiteroles, choux filled with cream and topped with chocolate, became popular in British restaurants in the second half of the 20th century and were for decades one of the most commonly ordered desserts. The key to choux is the vigorous beating of eggs into the hot paste: this creates the steam that makes the pastry hollow inside.

content.text: The choux paste must be beaten vigorously and the eggs added one at a time: the consistency is correct when the paste is thick and glossy and drops reluctantly from the spoon. Do not open the oven during baking: the steam inside the buns is what makes them rise and hollow. Poke a small hole in the base of each bun immediately after baking to let the steam escape, or the buns will go soggy.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Line two baking trays. Melt the 60 g butter in 150 ml water with the sugar and salt. Bring to a rolling boil. Remove from the heat. Tip in all the flour at once. Beat vigorously until the paste pulls away from the sides of the pan and is smooth and shiny. Leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time. The paste should be thick, glossy, and fall from the spoon in a slow ribbon.

Spoon or pipe walnut-sized mounds onto the trays. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and crisp. Do not open the oven. Immediately after removing, poke a small hole in the base of each bun. Cool on a rack.

Make the chocolate sauce: heat the 150 ml cream to just below a simmer. Pour over the chopped chocolate and 20 g butter. Stir until smooth. Whip the 400 ml cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks. Fill each bun through the hole in the base. Pile onto plates and pour over the warm chocolate sauce.
